svg.title: How conversation_search finds messages
svg.desc: Top, the rule of a self-hosted Letta server, four steps of plain code: keep the messages of every conversation that contain the whole query as one piece of text, ignoring case; order them newest first; keep the first five; drop tool messages, after the cut. The description the model reads promises a hybrid text and semantic search, which needs a hosted vector service. Bottom, the five queries the agent made before answering the question in the notebook: three long ones found nothing; 'restaurant recommendations' found one of the agent's own earlier replies; 'Kreuzberg' found four messages, three of them the agent's replies and one the user's message about the move. None returned anything that was not already in the memory block.
svg.text: The tool's description promises “hybrid search (text + semantic similarity)”. A self-hosted server, without a hosted vector
database, runs four steps of plain code instead.
Letta 0.16.8, self-hosted: plain code, no model call
whole query, as one piece of
So a list of keywords matches almost nothing, and a short query returns the newest messages that mention it: often the question itself and the

THE FIVE SEARCHES BEFORE THE ANSWER
Berlin Kreuzberg Indian restaurant paneer peanut
Everything the answer needed was already in the memory block. The searches added five model calls and nothing new.
